rows.evidence: Q1: Results section <U+2013> authors apply their own design methodology to two example networks (Albacete sprinkler zone; 127.7 ha citrus drip network in Valencia), running EPANET simulations, DIOPRAM pipe optimisation and energy-consumption calculations for pump combinations (Tables 3-9, Figs 5-6).
rows.notes: The study is a design-methodology paper with worked examples (model/design calculations never compared with field measurements). The statement that on-demand systems are expensive because of the conveyance capacity and flow control needed to meet peak demand appears only in the Introduction as a general assertion, not as a finding. The study's own results concern hydrant discharge sizing, maximum/minimum demand curves, and pumping-plant energy consumption and the cost of variable-speed drives; it reports no comparison of investment cost between on-demand and rotation/restricted-demand networks and no measurement of investment cost attributable to guaranteeing peak supply. It even notes that flow-limiting hydraulic valves reduce installation cost. Hence no own evidence on the claimed effect.

notes: Full text available; some equations and figure labels garbled by OCR but readable. Study is a methodological/design paper with illustrative applications rather than an empirical comparison of network types.
